dedupe_keys.name: swolfpy solid waste optimization life cycle framework in python

description: SwolfPy is an open-source Python framework that simulates the emissions, energy use and material use of a municipal solid waste (MSW) management system from collection to final disposal or recovery, and optimises how waste flows are allocated among processes. It ships default process models for landfill (including landfill gas, leachate and carbon storage), mass-burn waste-to-energy, gasification with syngas combustion, composting, home composting, anaerobic digestion, single-stream material recovery facilities, refuse-derived fuel production, reprocessing of recyclables, transfer stations, single-family, multi-family and commercial collection, and conversion of food waste to animal feed. Users build a custom treatment network, allocate waste fractions to processes, run comparative life-cycle assessment and contribution analysis, run built-in Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and minimise cost or environmental burden subject to technical and policy constraints such as landfill diversion targets. It was developed at North Carolina State University and is described in the Journal of Industrial Ecology (2022). Coverage is generic: any city or region can be modelled by supplying its waste generation, composition and process data; spatial detail is limited to the process network. It is a Python package on PyPI (version 1.4.0, March 2024) built on the Brightway2 LCA framework, with a desktop interface. Licence: GNU GPL version 2; free. Caveats: pinned, older dependency versions (Python 3.9 era, Brightway2 2.4) and no release since 2024. Simulation uses: capacity planning and optimisation of waste collection, treatment and disposal systems. Related tools: the Brightway LCA framework and openLCA, not yet catalogued.
